scenes.heading: Handling scope creep in consulting engagements

sents.d: Handling scope creep in consulting engagements
Clear scope boundaries protect profitability on fixed-fee consulting work.

Consulting engagements are especially prone to scope creep since deliverables are often less tangible than a physical product — a client's 'quick additional question' can quietly expand into significant unpaid extra work.

Defining specifically what's included in the engagement (which deliverables, how many revision or feedback rounds, what's explicitly out of scope) in the proposal or contract gives you language to reference when a request falls outside the agreement.

When a legitimate new request comes up mid-engagement, treating it as a change order — a specific additional scope and fee, agreed before doing the work — protects your margin without requiring an uncomfortable outright refusal.

take: Define scope up front and price new requests as change orders.
